articles.excerpt: A bug report lands in a team chat. Three people suggest fixes. Someone corrects the original report. Then you ask an AI coding assistant to handle it. Which version of the conversation did you just de…
articles.body: A bug report lands in a team chat. Three people suggest fixes. Someone corrects the original report. Then you ask an AI coding assistant to handle it. Which version of the conversation did you just delegate? On October 23, GitHub announced a consolidated GitHub app for Microsoft Teams , bringing notifications and Copilot into the same app. A notification can lead to an investigation and a pull request through a GitHub mention. The announcement still puts review, testing and merging with the team. That shorter handoff is useful. It also makes it easier to hand over a conversation before anyone has decided what it means. My recommendation is to insert a small decision snapshot between the chat and the coding task.

articles.title: Our feedback box's busiest tester turned out to be Google's test robot
articles.excerpt: We put a feedback button in every build we ship. Tap it, type a line, and the report arrives with the device model and the app version. Each report becomes a ticket, and each ticket starts a fix attem…
articles.body: We put a feedback button in every build we ship. Tap it, type a line, and the report arrives with the device model and the app version. Each report becomes a ticket, and each ticket starts a fix attempt. Then a trivia app we had just uploaded to Play got seven reports in a single day. The texts were ospuuq , pzxoim , caokah . Six lowercase letters each. All seven came from the same OnePlus 8 Pro, all on app version 1.0.0. It was not a person. It was the Play pre-launch report (Firebase Test Lab's Robo crawler), which taps every input it can find, types something, and presses the button next to it. It does this again on every upload. So for a day we had counted a crawler as our most active tester, and some of those tickets had already started fix attempts for a bug that did not exist.

articles.body: Updating the PHP runtime is not the same as updating WordPress. The core application may support the new version while an older plugin, a custom theme function, or an integration still assumes behavior from the previous runtime. The biggest mistake is treating a successful homepage load as a compatibility test. A typical site has code paths that do not run on the homepage: password reset, contact forms, scheduled jobs, payments, imports, and REST API callbacks. Here is a focused preflight process for maintaining a WordPress site with less guesswork. 1. Capture the baseline Before changing anything, note the current PHP version, WordPress core version, active theme, installed plugins, and the site's critical business workflows.

articles.excerpt: Email-enricher: 200 lines that replace a subscription Lead-gen platforms charge $49–$299 a month to rent you your own pipeline. I replaced the stack with five small Python scripts I own outright. What…
articles.body: Email-enricher: 200 lines that replace a subscription Lead-gen platforms charge $49–$299 a month to rent you your own pipeline. I replaced the stack with five small Python scripts I own outright. What it does. scrape_maps.py finds businesses by niche × city on free OpenStreetMap data, no API key. enrich_emails.py finds emails on business websites and verifies them before you send — the email-gate step most campaigns skip, then bounce for. dedupe_score.py dedupes and scores prospects into tiers A/B/C/D. write_opener.py drafts personalized first lines from one real fact per business. send_track.py sends from your own SMTP with SQLite tracking; unsubscribes honored. Honest math. 100 raw leads → ~20 worth emailing → 3–8% replies on a clean list. No "10,000 leads in 5 minutes".

articles.title: One Real Docstring a Night: A Local Open-Weight Model That Keeps a Streak Honest
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady streakkeeper is a nightly GitHub Action that makes one small, real documentation improvement to one of my re…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built streakkeeper is a nightly GitHub Action that makes one small, real documentation improvement to one of my repositories, then stops. It is scheduled for 22:30 every night. It wakes up, asks GitHub whether I have already contributed today, picks a repository, shallow-clones it, and walks the Python syntax tree for a docstring or README section that is missing or says nothing. A local open-weight model drafts the text. A second model reads the same code and decides whether the draft is true. If it is, the script proves the code did not change, commits one file, and goes back to sleep. The effort it saves is not typing.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 24, 1946: V-2 rocket takes 1st photos of Earth from space
articles.excerpt: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. While these grainy, black-and-white images might not look like much today, they were a huge deal at the time, because no one had ever seen Earth from space before. The V-2 rocket launched from the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. It carried a 35-millimeter motion picture camera that captured a new frame every second and a half. The rocket soared to an altitude of about 65 miles before falling back to Earth. Both the rocket and the camera were destroyed after crashing into the Earth at a speed of about 340 miles per hour. But the film survived because it was protected inside a steel case. Scientists had to drive out into the New Mexico desert to retrieve the film.

articles.body: It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of " Star Trek " before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say. That should trouble any Trekkie.

articles.title: Medusa's eye, Halloween fireballs and more: 5 skywatching targets to look out for this spooky season
articles.excerpt: Five spooky skywatching targets perfect for naked eye stargazing this Halloween!
articles.body: The spooky season is officially here! To celebrate, we've put together a list of five Halloween-themed skywatching targets that you can enjoy with nothing but the naked eye or binoculars and, of course, clear skies. Over millennia, the night sky has helped shape human beliefs. In return, we have imprinted our myths, stories and perceptions upon it, seeing monsters and mythology in the twinkling lights of the stars and assigning sinister aspects to innocent cosmic objects. Many of these ghostly impressions and meanings have survived to the present day. Here are a few of our favorites. The Pleiades open star cluster Don't be fooled by their beauty; the blue-white stars of the Pleiades are dripping in spooky lore.

At the time the comet-chasing spacecraft was about 472 million kilometers from planet Earth, but only 16 kilometers from the surface of comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko .
